summary: BF16 RMS normalization with optional offset gain or SiLU gate, rounded once or Llama-style
implementation_scope: CUDA row kernel, validated borrowed BF16 views, host formula and standalone native mode/shape/alias POC; engine quality/performance remain external

agent_guidance.use_when: Contiguous BF16 row normalization matches the engine formula and an optional gate belongs at its epilogue
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Views or formulas differ without adaptation, or an existing fused kernel already handles normalization efficiently
provides: CUDA FP32 row reduction with BF16 output and plain/unit-offset/gated modes
Selectable BF16 rounding order: once after gain (Gemma style) or normalized value first, then the gain product (HF Llama-family style)
Native shape, stride, workspace and alias validation
CMake target and executable Python formula reference
Host reference for folding split-reduction partials into the residual in a fixed order before normalizing (deterministic, no atomics)
engine_supplies: Device views, caller stream and lifetime/readiness integration
Native toolchain build and supported target configuration
Native numerical, alias, shape-boundary and performance validation
preserve: Gain convention, rounding order and epsilon placement
Declared input/output representations, supported aliases and view lifetime
Rounding and reduction behavior assessed under engine criteria
adapt: Kernel dispatch based on actual workload measurements

code_files.purpose: CUDA FP32 reduction and BF16 normalization/gated epilogue
Standalone native borrowed-view POC with independent BF16 oracle, both rounding orders, boundary and wide shapes, aliases and metadata rejection

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ for the formula; native source requires CMake 3.28+, C++/CUDA 20, the CUDA toolkit and a device compatible with the chosen build
requires.model: Row RMS normalization on BF16 input/gain/output; optional equal-shaped gate
requires.workload: Native source accepts width 1..2^24, rows 1..2^31-1 and contiguous two-byte elements

contract.input: BF16 device views, gain row, optional gate, positive FP32 epsilon, rounding order (default single) and caller stream
contract.output: Enqueued BF16 output plus Dispatch metadata
contract.ownership: Caller retains all device views until stream completion. Exact input/output or gate/output aliases are admitted; partial aliases and output/gain overlap are rejected.
contract.failure: Host validation rejects unsupported views, shapes, modes, epsilon, workspace and aliases before enqueue. Launch errors throw; caller handles physical settlement.
contract.core_boundary: Use core-owned device buffers and stream; normalization arithmetic remains a technique/consumer component.

dependencies: Python standard library for the formula
CMake 3.28+ and C++/CUDA 20 for native build
CUDA runtime and BF16 headers for native source

validation.host: Python formula fixtures and worked example cover modes, rounding orders, BF16 rounding, shapes, finite values and gain conventions; no CUDA execution
validation.native: Standalone CUDA example checks 238 bounded finite mode/rounding/shape/alias cases (widths to 16384, rows to 65537) against an independent double/BF16 formula, 9 exact normalize_first rounding-order cases at widths 4096-16384, width/row limits and metadata rejection; extreme numerical ranges, full-model quality and speed require consumer evidence
validation.performance: Unmeasured for a native engine; host fixture success is not a speed claim
